headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers, by requiring them to pay for increased generating capacity.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users, utility companies.
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to Users.
news_summary: New legislation in Virginia requires data centers using 25 MW or more to pay for increased generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed on to other customers. This aims to protect residential ratepayers from rising utility bills driven by data center demand.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandate
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency on their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservation advocates, transparency advocates.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Data Center Water Use Tracking.
news_summary: Virginia's General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report the total volume of water supplied to data centers. This legislation aims to provide better data on data center water consumption and promote responsible resource management.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Regulations
short_summary: This bill grants local governments more control over data center siting by requiring site assessments for noise, water, and other impacts near residential areas and schools.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, developers, pro-business groups.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Requires Data Center Site Assessments.
news_summary: HB 153, passed by the General Assembly, requires local governments to conduct site assessments for new high-energy data centers. These assessments will measure noise levels and evaluate impacts on water supply and other critical factors near residential communities and schools.
